q: What is the energy and fuel mix of the Pune aluminium casting cluster?
title: Pune aluminium casting: the energy mix
short: Furnace oil and grid power, with little else. TERI's profile of Pune's 50 or so casting units counts 44,153 kL of furnace oil and 350 million kWh a year, about 77,500 toe in all: 61% thermal for melting, 39% electricity. On today's factors that is roughly 377,000 t CO2.
audience: Aluminium die casting units in Pimpri-Chinchwad, Bhosari, Chakan and nearby estates around Pune

sections.h: Eight large units set the number
ul: 12 micro units (up to 100 t a year) make about 1,500 t together.
30 small and medium units (100 to 5,000 t) make about 54,000 t.
8 large units (above 5,000 t) make about 3,40,000 t, close to 86% of the cluster's capacity of 3,95,500 t.
About 35 of the 50 units sit in Pimpri-Chinchwad-Bhosari MIDC and Chakan MIDC.
Electricity: 350 million kWh (30,063 toe). It runs holding furnaces, PDC and GDC machines, core shooters, shot blasting, machining and compressors in every unit, whatever the melting furnace.
Furnace oil: 44,153 kL (43,579 toe), mostly in skalner, tower and crucible melting furnaces.
Diesel: 2,592 kL (2,536 toe), for DG sets during load shedding in Bhosari and Chakan.
Natural gas: 1.206 million scm (1,025 toe). LPG: 210 t (263 toe), partly for die heating on GDC and LPDC lines.

sections.h: Energy share and carbon share are not the same
p: Electricity is 39% of the energy but close to two thirds of the CO2, because each kWh on India's grid carries more carbon than the oil that would give the same heat. A unit that melts in an oil skalner and does everything else on power usually finds its electricity bill, not its oil bill, drives the footprint its OEM sees.

sections.h: Using the cluster figure for your own unit
p: Don't. A micro unit with an electric crucible and a large unit with a tower furnace have almost nothing in common. Add up your own furnace oil, gas, LPG, diesel and kWh for twelve months and divide by tonnes of good castings shipped.

example.title: Cluster CO2 on today's factors (estimate)
lines: Electricity: 350 million kWh x 0.675 kg = 236,250 t CO2
Furnace oil: 44,153 kL x 2.97 t = 131,134 t CO2
Diesel: 2,592 kL x 2.645 t = 6,856 t CO2
Natural gas: 1.206 million scm x 2.05 kg = 2,472 t CO2
Total about 377,300 t, or about 0.95 t CO2 per tonne of capacity
example.note: Quantities from TERI's cluster profile (2014 data). Grid factor CEA FY 2025-26; fuels IPCC 2006. The aluminium you melt carries its own, much larger footprint and is not included.

senseible: If your castings go to the EU under a covered code, Senseible's CBAM tools work from the same furnace oil, gas and diesel invoices; your electricity bills are read into monthly records for the OEM footprint, which counts power.
